title: Positional Parameter Overload (Large Parameter List)
damaged_code:
```rust
fn create_user(
    first_name: String,
    last_name: String,
    email: String,
    phone: String,
    street: String,
    city: String,
    zip_code: String,
    is_admin: bool,
    send_welcome_email: bool,
) -> Result<User, Error> {
    todo!()
}
```
pattern: A function signature accepting a large list (typically 6-7+) of individual primitive arguments, especially of identical types (like consecutive `String`s or `bool`s).
why_bad: Call sites are incredibly unreadable and highly fragile. It is extremely easy to accidentally swap two positional parameters of the same type (like swapping `first_name` and `last_name`, or `street` and `city`) without triggering any compiler errors. Adding a single field breaks every call site across the codebase.
detection: Identify any public function or method accepting more than 5 positional arguments, especially when several consecutive arguments share the exact same primitive type.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. Low-level library constructors or internal wrapper interfaces where positional mapping is strictly isolated to a single calling file.
fix: Group related parameters into cohesive parameter structs or apply the Builder pattern.
source: *Steve McConnell - Code Complete (2004)*, Chapter 7, "High-Quality Routines" (Limit parameters to about 7); *Martin Fowler - Refactoring (1999)*, Chapter 3, "Long Parameter List"; *Vaughn Vernon - Implementing Domain-Driven Design (2013)*, Chapter 10.
